- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-0.3) or shows sharp decline, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 3–8% for 3–7 days ahead.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–3% for 2–5 days after spike.  
- If 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend in history + negative sentiment, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 1–3% upward bias for 5–10 days ahead.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 18-day average for first 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/–0.5+), model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of last 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
